function: Joint ISAC-BS transmit beamforming, STAR-IRS amplitude and phase design, and SCMA codebook and subcarrier allocation, maximizing energy efficiency under a sensing beam-pattern error limit (pp. 7-8).
system: Downlink multi-user MISO ISAC at THz: BS with NBS=5 antennas, 2 single-antenna users, STAR-IRS (simultaneously transmitting and reflecting) NS=4, SCMA J=4 subcarriers, C=6 codebooks (pp. 4, 10).
method: Meta-DDPG: DDPG actor-critic with a meta-critic (bi-level meta-learning), trained by reinforcement learning with a hybrid constraint-penalty reward and quantized discrete actions (pp. 8-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: Rician channels (LoS plus NLoS rays) with THz free-space and molecular-absorption path loss, deterministic coefficients; no standard model, dataset or measurement (pp. 5-6, 10).
test_conditions: Each setting (learning rate, multiple access, Pmax, users, D, CSI error) has its own learning curve; no model trained in one setting is tested in another (pp. 10-14).
baselines: Non-learned: convex optimization (AO, Dinkelbach, CVX), uniform and random beamforming. Learned: DDPG, PPO, TD3, SAC, hybrid MDRL plus Q-learning (Figs. 6, 8-9, pp. 11-13).
metrics: Reward, energy efficiency, total sum rate and total consumed power versus episodes; EE versus D and users; running time and complexity (Figs. 3-11, pp. 10-14).
complexity: Time complexity in FLOPS: Meta-DDPG O(484750) vs DDPG O(464700), Fig. 7; running time 1502.36 s vs 3969.63 s for the convex benchmark, Fig. 10 (pp. 10, 12-13).
q1_support: p. 5: "The channel coefficients are modeled as Rician channels." Path loss is a custom THz model (pp. 5-6); no 3GPP model, dataset or measurement is used.
q2_support: p. 11: "The figures are obtained for P max values of 5, 10, 30, and 50 Watts." Each value has its own learning curve; no trained model is tested in an unseen setting, and the adaptation claim on p. 4 is not tested.
q3_support: p. 11: "our proposed MDRL, PPO, TD3, SAC, DDPG, uniform beamforming, random beamforming, and Q-learning"; p. 13: "MDRL outperforms the convex optimization benchmark" (EE, Figs. 8-9).
q4_support: p. 12: "The time complexity of the Meta-DDPG algorithm is O(484750)"; p. 13: running time 1502.36 s versus 3969.63 s for the convex benchmark.
q5_support: p. 10: "We utilized PyTorch version 1.4.0 for the implementation of Meta-DDPG and DDPG algorithms"; no code or data link appears anywhere in the paper, and channels come from its own simulator.
notes: Identity checked: p. 1 header 'DOI 10.1109/TWC.2025.3580347' and title match; file is the accepted author manuscript. Area 5 rather than 3: the system is ISAC and sensing enters only through the beam-pattern error constraint C1 (p. 7; three desired beams of width 10 degrees, p. 6); the reviewer may confirm. q3: plain DDPG is the base of Meta-DDPG and could be read as an ablation, but PPO, TD3 and SAC are separate standard learning algorithms applied to the same problem (Fig. 6, pp. 11-12). q2: pp. 4 and 8 claim that meta-learning adapts to new environments, but no experiment tests it. The carrier frequency is never given as a number, only 'THz band'. STAR-IRS size is NS elements (p. 4) or NS x NS (p. 5); Table II gives NS=4.
